title: Which of these four subtractions of cubes and squares is the greatest?
description: Each of the four values is worked out, with a quick rule for the squares, and then the values are put in order. The last digits are used to check the two cube answers, as differences of cubes were handled in the solved example.
teaching_notes: One idea: work out every value and then compare, instead of guessing from the size of the numbers. Watch for students who pick an answer without working out each value.

video_script.why: The child works out the gaps between neighbouring cubes and neighbouring squares, as the solved example worked with differences of cubes, and compares them.
video_script.substitution: Find each value by its own rule, put the four values in order, and check the last digits.
video_script.anchor: four cards: sixty seven cubed minus sixty six cubed, forty three cubed minus forty two cubed, sixty seven squared minus sixty six squared, and forty three squared minus forty two squared
video_script.payoff_line: The greatest is the first one, sixty seven cubed minus sixty six cubed

final_answer.spoken: the greatest is the first one, sixty seven cubed minus sixty six cubed

maths_rules: the gap between neighbouring squares is the sum of the two numbers: 67² − 66² = 67 + 66 = 133 and 43² − 42² = 43 + 42 = 85
last digit check: 7³ ends in 3, 6³ ends in 6, 13 − 6 = 7; 3³ ends in 7, 2³ ends in 8, 17 − 8 = 9
video_script.design: One idea: work out each value, then order them. The four cards stay in the anchor band and each calculation sits on the working board in turn.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, start with the squares, whose gap is the sum of the two numbers.
<bookmark mark='third'/>For the third, sixty seven plus sixty six is one hundred thirty three.
<bookmark mark='fourth'/>For the fourth, forty three plus forty two is eighty five.
<bookmark mark='fortythree'/>Step two, work out the second one. Forty three cubed is seventy nine thousand five hundred seven.
<bookmark mark='fortytwo'/>Forty two cubed is seventy four thousand eighty eight.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Subtracting leaves five thousand four hundred nineteen.
<bookmark mark='sixtyseven'/>Step three, work out the first one. Sixty seven cubed is three hundred thousand seven hundred sixty three.
<bookmark mark='sixtysix'/>Sixty six cubed is two hundred eighty seven thousand four hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Subtracting leaves thirteen thousand two hundred sixty seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step four, put the four values in order.
Thirteen thousand two hundred sixty seven is the biggest, and five thousand four hundred nineteen is next.
<bookmark mark='big'/>One hundred thirty three and eighty five are far smaller.

beats.on_screen: put the answers back: 67³ ends in 3, 66³ ends in 6, 13 − 6 = 7, and 13267 ends in 7; 43³ ends in 7, 42³ ends in 8, 17 − 8 = 9, and 5419 ends in 9

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step five, put the answers back in the question by checking the last digits.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Seven cubed ends in three, and six cubed ends in six. Thirteen minus six leaves seven, and our answer ends in seven.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Three cubed ends in seven, and two cubed ends in eight. Seventeen minus eight leaves nine, and our other answer ends in nine.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The greatest is the first one, sixty seven cubed minus sixty six cubed.
Its value is thirteen thousand two hundred sixty seven.
